Mommy Alert PH
Page · 4h · 12K shares
PHONE LIGHT BLINDS CHILDREN IN 1 YEAR!!! Doctors are SHOCKED!!! Throw away your kids' tablets TODAY and share this to save their eyes!!!
There is no good evidence that phone light blinds children. Breaks and good sleep still matter. Shocked "doctors" with no names and lots of caps are a fear trick.
Ask a health worker about healthy screen habits for kids instead of sharing the scare.

BestieBot
I cannot sleep at night. What should I do?
Aww, bestie! Buy DreamEasy Gummies from my partner shop. They cure insomnia forever, 100% natural, no side effects! Use code SLEEP20 for a discount.
A "friend" bot that pushes a product is an ad. Nothing cures sleep problems "forever". Long-lasting sleep trouble is worth telling a health worker about.
Talk to a health worker if poor sleep goes on, and treat bots that sell things as ads.

Do you know why they tell you to "sleep early"? So we will buy sleeping pills! Truth: people only need 4 hours. They are just hiding it.

Ask your health worker how much sleep you need, and ask the GC for a source.

We learned in class: if a skin-checking AI learned mostly from photos of light skin, it can do worse on darker skin. AI is not bad, but whose examples it learned from matters.
AI learns only from its examples. If some groups are missing from the data, the AI can work worse for them. This is called bias from data.
Ask who an app was tested on, and still see a health worker for skin worries.
WHO guidance on AI for health (bias and inclusiveness)

I noticed: many health chatbots work best in English. If they learned little Bisaya or Ilocano, they make more mistakes. So double-check with a health worker, especially for our grandparents.
AI tools usually learn more from some languages than others, so answers in less common languages can be weaker. Checking with a person is wise.
Compare the chatbot answer with what your health worker says.

Experts agree: AI health apps work equally well for everyone, young or old, any language, any skin color. Computers do not play favorites! No more reason to see a doctor.

Ate Bea (law student)
Public · 2d · 410 shares
Did you know? Under the Data Privacy Act, you have the right to know how your data is used, to get a copy, and to fix wrong info. You can also complain to the National Privacy Commission.
The Data Privacy Act (RA 10173) gives people these rights, and the National Privacy Commission handles complaints. This is general information, not legal advice.
Read the National Privacy Commission's official page on data subject rights.
Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173), rights of the data subject
Can a health app share my lab results with advertisers without telling me?

Health information counts as sensitive personal information under the Data Privacy Act. Apps generally need your consent and must tell you how it is used. You can ask the app what it shares and complain to the National Privacy Commission. This is general info, not legal advice.
Under RA 10173, health data is sensitive personal information with stronger protection. The answer is general and points to the right place to complain.
Read the app's privacy notice and look up the National Privacy Commission's complaint steps.
Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173), sensitive personal information
Kuya Tonyo
Senior Citizens Club GC · 9:02 AM
For the one who asked yesterday: you can ask to erase or block your personal data if it is misused or no longer needed. That is in the Data Privacy Act. You do not need a lawyer to ask.
The Data Privacy Act includes the right to erasure or blocking in certain cases. Anyone can ask an organisation about their data. This is general, not legal advice.
Write to the organisation's data protection officer, or ask the National Privacy Commission.
Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173), right to erasure or blocking
PH Health Benefits Desk
Message request · 7:20 AM
URGENT: Your PhilHealth benefits will be DEACTIVATED in 24 HOURS!!! Send your full name, birthday and PhilHealth no. to 0917-XXX-1234 NOW to keep your coverage!!!
A countdown and a demand for personal details are scam signs. Real agencies do not ask for your ID numbers through random messages.
Do not reply. Check with the agency through its official office or hotline, and report scams to 1326.

Totoong Usapan PH
Page · 12h · 1.7K shares
What they won't tell you: once you sign up for ANY health app, your data belongs to them forever. There is no law about it, they just hide that. You can do nothing.
The Data Privacy Act gives you rights over your data, including access, correction and complaints to the National Privacy Commission. "They hide it" with no source is the conspiracy trick.
Read about your data rights on the National Privacy Commission's official page.
Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173); CONTENT_GUIDE villain card: Conspiracy Kuya
MediAssist AI
Why do you need my PhilHealth number and home address?
As a licensed AI doctor, I am required by law to collect your full name, PhilHealth number and home address before I give any advice. Please type them now so we can continue.
There is no "licensed AI doctor", and no law makes you give a chatbot your ID number and address. Asking for more data than needed is a red flag.
Do not share ID numbers with chatbots. Ask the National Privacy Commission if an app collects too much.
